generator: tools/atom/build_elements.py (inputs fetched by tools/atom/fetch_sources.py; checked by tools/atom/check_elements.py)

config, subshells, ground_level.source: NIST Atomic Spectra Database, 'Ground levels and ionization energies for the neutral atoms' (Z = 1-108)
config, subshells, ground_level.note: Z = 109-118 are predictions (Wikipedia 'Electron configurations of the elements (data page)', which cites the CRC Handbook); config_predicted is true for Z >= 103 because none of these has been measured spectroscopically. For Ds and Rg the CRC Handbook gives 6d9 7s1 and 6d10 7s1 instead.

ionization_eV, ionization_unc_eV, ioniza.source: same NIST table; status from NIST's brackets: ( ) interpolated/extrapolated, [ ] theoretical

mass, mass_note.source: CIAAW standard atomic weights 2021 (abridged = conventional values where CIAAW gives an interval); elements without stable isotopes: mass of the longest-lived isotope from NUBASE2020 mass excess

isotopes, mostAbundantA, data/atomic/iso.source: NUBASE2020: F.G. Kondev, M. Wang, W.J. Huang, S. Naimi, G. Audi, Chin. Phys. C 45, 030001 (2021). Abundances: CIAAW representative isotopic composition where CIAAW gives a single value; NUBASE2020 'IS' value where CIAAW gives an interval (the value is checked to lie inside it).
isotopes, mostAbundantA, data/atomic/iso.note: Elements without a natural isotope list the longest-lived known ground state with a measured (not extrapolated) half-life. For Z >= 104 these rest on a handful of atoms. Lithium uses the NIST representative composition 0.0759 / 0.9241 (CIAAW gives only the interval 0.019-0.078 for Li-6, and the NUBASE value 0.0485 does not reproduce the standard atomic weight). For every other element the abundance-weighted isotope mass was recomputed and is within 4e-4 of the standard atomic weight (B and S lie inside their CIAAW intervals).

data/atomic/zeff.json.source: Clementi & Raimondi, J. Chem. Phys. 38, 2686 (1963) (Z <= 36); Clementi, Raimondi & Reinhardt, J. Chem. Phys. 47, 1300 (1967) (Z = 37-86), as tabulated in the mendeleev Python package; Slater, Phys. Rev. 36, 57 (1930) rules implemented in build_elements.py for Z > 86 and any subshell missing from the tables.
data/atomic/zeff.json.note: These are screening constants of single Slater-type orbitals. They are NOT used to draw the clouds (cloud sizes come from data/atomic/scf.json); they are kept for the effective-nuclear-charge card.

data/atomic/lines.json (hydrogen).source: Computed from the Rydberg formula with R_H = R_inf/(1 + m_e/m_p); R_inf = 10 973 731.568160 /m and m_e/m_p = 1/1836.15267343 (CODATA 2018). Air wavelengths use the Edlen (1966) refractive index of standard air.

data/atomic/lines.json (others).source: NIST Atomic Spectra Database, lines form, neutral atoms (I), 380-780 nm, observed wavelength in air where listed else the Ritz wavelength; strongest 12 by listed relative intensity

electronegativity.source: Pauling scale as tabulated in the CRC Handbook / WebElements (read via Wikipedia 'Electronegativities of the elements (data page)'); mendeleev package where they agree. Values for Am-No are estimates in that table.

melt_K, boil_K.source: mendeleev package, corrected from the CRC Handbook / Lange values listed on Wikipedia 'Melting points of the elements (data page)' and 'Boiling points of the elements (data page)' and cross-checked against the PubChem periodic table; estimates and lower bounds left empty (see tools/atom/overrides.json). Hydrogen: PubChem triple-point value 13.81 K.

density.source: Gases at 0 C and 101.325 kPa (PubChem periodic table, agreeing within about 0.5% with Wikipedia 'Densities of the elements (data page)'); solids from the mendeleev package, checked there for Am, Bk, Cf, Es. No source found for Fr and Z >= 100: empty.

radius_vdw_pm, radius_vdw_source.source: Bondi 1964 where it exists, else Alvarez, Dalton Trans. 42, 8617 (2013); both via the mendeleev package. Spot-checked against Wikipedia 'Atomic radii of the elements (data page)' (Bondi column) for H, C, N, O, Cu, Ag, Au, Pb, Xe.

radius_covalent_pm.source: Cordero et al., Dalton Trans. 2008, 2832 (single-bond radii), via the mendeleev package, checked against the Cordero column on Wikipedia 'Covalent radius' for C (sp3 76 / sp2 73 / sp 69), Mn (139 low-spin / 161 high-spin), Fe (132 / 152) and Co (126 / 150): the stored values are the sp2 value for C and the average of the two spin states for Mn, Fe, Co; the card says so. Pyykko 2009 (calculated) where Cordero has none (Bk onwards); the card says 'calculated'.

radius_atomic_pm.source: 'Empirical' atomic radii as compiled in the mendeleev package (agree with the Slater 1964 column on Wikipedia for H, C, N, O, Fe, Cu, Ag, Au, Pb, U). Rough guide only. He, Ne and Ar are removed: the He 120 and Ne 160 entries on that page are marked 'citation needed' and Ar 71 is a calculated (Clementi, Raimondi and Reinhardt 1967) value; Kr and Xe have none, so no noble gas has an empirical radius here.

discovered.source: mendeleev package, corrected from Wikipedia 'Timeline of chemical element discoveries' where they disagreed (see discovered_note). 'Discovery' is partly a matter of definition: first recognised, first isolated, or first confirmed.

category, group, period, block, color_cp.source: mendeleev package; group/block adjusted so that Lu and Lr sit in group 3 (d block) and La-Yb, Ac-No are f block with no group. phase_stp is the state at room temperature; 'unknown' where no macroscopic sample has been observed.

summary.source: Written for this project (tools/atom/summaries.json). Isotope and half-life statements in them were checked against NUBASE2020.

data/atomic/scf.json.source: Computed here: tools/atom/scf.py (non-relativistic spherical self-consistent-field atom, Kohn-Sham/Gaspar local exchange, no correlation) run by tools/atom/build_scf.py for the NIST ground-state configuration of every element.
data/atomic/scf.json.validation: Compared with numerical Hartree-Fock <r> from Table 11 of J. B. Mann, Atomic Structure Calculations II, Los Alamos report LA-3691 (1968), https://www.osti.gov/biblio/4553157 (text layer of the scanned report read by tools/atom/parse_mann.py). The statistics are stored in scf.json under 'validation'.
data/atomic/scf.json.note: Relativity is not included; relativity contracts s and p shells and expands d and f shells, most strongly at gold in its row (P. Pyykkö and J.-P. Desclaux, Acc. Chem. Res. 12, 276 (1979)). No number is quoted for the size of the contraction because none was checked against the paper.
